rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a fair-quality blastocyst and acknowledges image blur, but it overstates confidence in ICM/TE assessment from this soft single frame and introduces possible 4BB interpretation despite provided 3BB.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, male-factor context, endometrium, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo grade to frame prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimates tied to embryo grade and favorable patient factors; only minor uncertainty around fresh-transfer receptivity effects.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based and consistent with standard IVF practice, including SET at age 31 and avoiding unsupported add-ons; minor issue is some speculative discussion without cycle hormone data.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management, OHSS monitoring, luteal support, when not to over-investigate, and future-cycle considerations such as freeze-all or selective PGT-A discussion.
